Job Description

The Role:

Global Manufacturing Electrical & SDV is seeking curious, driven students who want to be part of something bigger than themselves. If you're energized by real challenges, eager to learn, and ready to contribute to meaningful work that shapes the future of the automotive industry, this opportunity is for you.

This isn’t just about getting experience—it’s about making an impact. You’ll work alongside experienced professionals, gain hands-on exposure to cutting-edge projects, and see firsthand how your ideas can influence real-world outcomes. You’ll face fast-paced environments and evolving priorities, but you’ll also have the support of a people-first culture that values growth, learning, and balance.

If you're excited to build your skills, expand your perspective, and contribute to something with real purpose, we’d love to hear from you.

The Team:

Global Manufacturing Electrical & SDV helps GM build high-quality vehicles to our customers by combining electrical engineering, software, data, testing, and manufacturing expertise. Our team works to improve Electrical First-Time Quality, solve plant-critical challenges, and develop scalable solutions. We bring manufacturing software and hardware design in-house to move faster and enable Vehicle as a Tester (VaaT) and SDV 2.0 capabilities. Interns will gain hands-on experience solving real manufacturing problems and contributing to innovations that will shape the future of vehicle production.

What You’ll Do:

As a student in the Global Manufacturing Electrical & SDV organization, you will focus on delivering innovative manufacturing solutions that help support electrical first-time quality (E-FTQ) at our plants. You will:

- Help drive meaningful progress in vehicle electrical systems through hands-on projects and problem-solving.

- Foster a forward-thinking work culture that embraces change and navigates future organizational and industry challenges.

- Build and nurture strategic relationships across various functions including software, manufacturing, and program management to synergize efforts towards future innovations.

Examples of past intern projects include:

- Assist with writing manufacturing software code (using C++) that supports the next generation of vehicle electrical systems.

- Build easy-to-understand dashboards using Power BI to help manufacturing and engineering teams make data-driven decisions and solve the customer and plants’ biggest problems.

- Help design innovative electrical tooling and equipment solutions that empower assembly plants to ensure the highest quality vehicle electrical systems and create the standardized work for use of this hardware.

- Designing and documenting a scalable test setup that provides shared power and network connections for vehicle electronic components.

Required Qualifications:

- Pursuit of a bachelor’s or master’s degree in engineering or technology in one of the following areas: Automotive, Computer/Computer Science/Computer Animation, Construction Management, Civil, Industrial, Industrial Operations, Information Technology, Machine Learning, Manufacturing, Mechanical, Mechatronics, Robotics, Software, Data Scientists, or equivalent field

- Must be graduating between December 2027 and June 2010

- Able to work fulltime, 40 hours per week during the summer months

What will give you a Competitive Edge (Preferred Qualifications):

- Insatiable curiosity and desire to learn

- Demonstrated leadership in academic, extracurricular, or project settings

- Conceptual understanding and/or experience in any of the following:

- Manufacturing processes

- Programming or understanding software logic (e.g., Linux, C++)

- Information Technology systems

- Ability to work independently and with a team

- Effective communication and relationship-building skills

- High level of integrity, self-motivation, and adaptability in a fast-paced environment

GM does not provide immigration-related sponsorship for this role. Do not apply for this role if you will need GM immigration sponsorship now or in the future. This includes direct company sponsorship, entry of GM as the immigration employer of record on a government form, and any work authorization requiring a written submission or other immigration support from the company (e.g., H1-B, OPT, STEM OPT, CPT, TN, J-1, etc.)

About Rippling

Rippling gives businesses one place to run HR, IT, and Finance. It brings together all of the workforce systems that are normally scattered across a company, like payroll, expenses, benefits, and computers. For the first time ever, you can manage and automate every part of the employee lifecycle in a single system.

Take onboarding, for example. With Rippling, you can hire a new employee anywhere in the world and set up their payroll, corporate card, computer, benefits, and even third-party apps like Slack and Microsoft 365—all within 90 seconds.

Based in San Francisco, CA, Rippling has raised $1.4B+ from the world’s top investors—including Kleiner Perkins, Founders Fund, Sequoia, Greenoaks, and Bedrock—and was named one of America's best startup employers by Forbes.

As an Engineering Intern, you will join one of our many teams in Summer 2027 (May/June-August/September) to develop robust, well-designed products, implement new updates and features, and solve complex problems that affect our business and our clients. Rippling Interns gain the experience of full-time engineers with responsibilities, ownership, and opportunity. Interns will be assigned projects that not only have an impact on the business, but that are also scoped to fit within the time constraints of their internship so they can see the full impact of their work.

We provide our interns exciting and innovative projects to work on that allow them to see the fruition of their work. During your 13 weeks at Rippling, we will provide all of the tools needed to be successful. Your dedicated mentor and manager will provide support for your learning and development throughout your time with us. You will join your fellow interns in a variety of socials, talks with Rippling leaders, and more!

Our goal is to identify exceptional emerging engineers who can continue their careers at Rippling after graduation, growing into full-time contributors on our team.

Note that this is a full stack software internship role! This means you will be working in the front end and the back end.

- Utilize your software engineering experience to tackle important projects, solving problems, and developing quality code
- Think critically and apply your knowledge to real world, complex problems
- Actively participate in team meetings to scope, drive, and progress your projects

- Foster relationships with your intern cohort and teams through both exclusive internship social events and company/office-wide events

About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

The Avionics team builds and supports the electronics that help Zipline’s aircraft sense, compute, communicate, and fly reliably. Field Systems Engineering connects that design work with what happens across the operating fleet. We investigate failures, use flight data and hands-on testing to understand their causes, and work with engineers and operators to improve the product. Our work spans hardware, software, and day-to-day operations, so we learn directly from the people maintaining and flying the aircraft.

The Role

As a Field Systems Engineering intern, you’ll help solve real problems affecting Zipline’s aircraft in the field. You’ll work with flight data, test hardware, and collaborate with engineers and operations teams to understand how avionics systems perform outside the lab. You’ll have a mentor and a project you can own, with opportunities to present your findings and see how they inform engineering decisions.

What You'll Do

- Investigate avionics issues using telemetry, logs, physical inspection, and bench tests.

- Analyze fleet data to identify patterns in system performance and reliability.

- Build or improve scripts, dashboards, or diagnostic tools that make issues easier to detect and understand.

- Help design and run tests to check possible failure causes and proposed fixes.

- Work with design engineers, technicians, and operators to learn how systems behave in practice.

- Document your methods, results, and recommendations so others can act on them.

What You'll Bring

- Currently pursuing a degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, aerospace engineering, robotics, computer science, or a related field.

- Experience with hands-on technical projects involving hardware, software, or both.

- Ability to analyze data or logs using Python, SQL, MATLAB, or a similar tool.

- Curiosity about how complex systems fail and a methodical approach to finding answers.

- Clear communication and willingness to learn from engineers, technicians, and operators.

- Must be proficient and comfortable with using and building AI tools

Nice to Have

- Experience using CAD software to design, modify, or inspect mechanical parts and assemblies.

- Hands-on experience building, testing, and debugging a physical system, such as through Formula SAE, Baja SAE, a robotics team, research, or a personal project.

What Else You Should Know

This internship is a full-time position, in-person at our South San Francisco office. We will host our Spring 2027 interns from January to April.

Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements.
